issues.description: Function name mismatch for the tensor-network zero-state constructor: the problem statement (and the solution implementation) refer to create_zero_state(num_qubits), but the template repository provides a different identifier init_zero_state(num_qubits). Problem statement and tests expect a function named create_zero_state with the specified signature; the template's init_zero_state signature exists but under a different name. This inconsistency will confuse students and cause tests or autograding that call create_zero_state to fail unless they rename or add an adapter, preventing straightforward use of the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template API match the problem statement and solution. Either (a) rename the template stub init_zero_state to create_zero_state with the same signature and behavior, or (b) add a small adapter in the template: define create_zero_state(num_qubits) that simply returns init_zero_state(num_qubits). Ensure the docstring and return type (list of rank-3 tensors: (1,2,1) per site) match the problem description so tests invoking create_zero_state succeed.

issues.description: The concept is the creation of the all-zero MPS (the n-qubit |0...0> initial state). The problem statement (task for Tensor Networks) explicitly asks students to implement create_zero_state(...). The solution implementation defines create_zero_state(...) (solution_repository/tensor_networks.py). However, the template starter code declares a stub named init_zero_state(...) (template_repository/tensor_networks.py). This mismatch (create_zero_state vs init_zero_state) maps to the same conceptual entity but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can prevent a student from locating the expected function to implement and increases cognitive load when matching requirements to the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Preferred options: (A) Rename the template stub init_zero_state(...) to create_zero_state(...) so the template matches the problem statement and solution; or (B) if init_zero_state(...) is intentionally preferred, update the problem statement and the solution to reference init_zero_state(...). Option (A) is recommended to minimize changes to the problem statement and solution.
